summary: Six destinations proposed (Albany, Torndirrup National Park, Denmark, Walpole Wilderness, Stirling Range National Park, Fitzgerald River National Park); 47 spots inside them and 9 standalone spots. 67 keeps: 7 kept entries became destinations or their base/container, 2 merged as duplicates, 2 long trails placed in wa-south-west. 22 reviews listed, not placed.

new_destinations.name: Albany

name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage has its own town page 'Albany (Western Australia)'; Tourism WA's Great Southern region page names Albany as the region's city.

new_destinations.reason: The region's city and main base (Wikivoyage page, Tourism WA): its own museums, fort and beaches plus the day-trip parks and beaches around King George Sound (Two Peoples Bay, Gull Rock, West Cape Howe), all reached from the city. Span 40 km (75% = 30 km) holds Little Beach at about 29 km, the farthest spot; Cheynes Beach (about 50 km) stays standalone. Torndirrup National Park, 7-8 km south, is its own destination (every national park with four or more spots is), so Albany keeps the city's own attractions.
new_destinations.needs: Proposal only: description, reasons by popularity with photos, tips, best months and a header (Pipeline C); coordinates to confirm.

new_destinations.name: Torndirrup National Park
new_destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Torndirrup National Park (park reference point on Frenchman Bay Road; confirm a visitor hub such as The Gap car park)

name_evidence.wording: DBCA park page 'Torndirrup National Park'; Australia's South West listing 'Torndirrup National Park'.

new_destinations.reason: A national park with seven kept spots (The Gap and Natural Bridge, Misery Beach, Blowholes, Salmon Holes, Stony Hill, Bald Head Walk Trail, Jimmy Newells): a destination in its own right, the Whanganui-National-Park pattern beside Albany. All spots within about 11 km of the reference point (75% of 24 km = 18 km).
new_destinations.needs: Proposal only: description, reasons by popularity with photos, tips, best months and a header (Pipeline C); coordinates to confirm.

new_destinations.name: Denmark

name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage town page 'Denmark (Western Australia)'; Tourism WA's Great Southern page names Denmark.

new_destinations.reason: Town on Wilson Inlet that visitors base in for William Bay National Park (Greens Pool, Elephant Rocks), Ocean Beach and Lights Beach: five kept spots, all within about 15 km. William Bay NP has only three spots of its own (Greens Pool, Elephant Rocks, Lights Beach) so it cannot be a destination; it is a spot of Denmark at its own visitor point. Category 'beach' because the draws are the coast; the owner may prefer 'city'.
new_destinations.needs: Proposal only: description, reasons by popularity with photos, tips, best months and a header (Pipeline C); coordinates to confirm.

new_destinations.name: Walpole Wilderness
new_destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Walpole, Western Australia (the base town and visitor centre)

name_evidence.wording: The Walpole Visitor Centre's Explore page calls the area 'the Walpole Wilderness' ('Rising above the Walpole Wilderness, Mount Frankland...', 'At the heart of the Walpole Wilderness, this tranquil marine park...') and lists Conspicuous Cliff, Peaceful Bay, Circular Pool, Fernhook Falls, Mount Frankland and Mandalay Beach under it; Wikipedia has 'Walpole Wilderness Area'. DBCA names Walpole as Walpole-Nornalup NP's base.

new_destinations.reason: The named region (COVERAGE 'Prefer the region travellers name') covering Walpole-Nornalup NP and the parks around Walpole that the visitor centre groups as the Walpole Wilderness. Seven kept spots here (Tree Top Walk, Giant Tingle Tree, Conspicuous Cliff, Circular Pool, Coalmine Beach, Peaceful Bay, Mount Clare), all within about 20 km of Walpole. Walpole town (kept) is the base and centre, described in the description, not a wrapper spot. Walpole-Nornalup NP (kept) is the container: every one of its named sites is a spot, so the park is not listed beside them. The span (32 km, reach 24 km) also holds three wa-south-west standalones the visitor centre lists under the same name (Mandalay Beach 19 km, Fernhook Falls 22 km, Mount Frankland NP): see cross_region_notes.
new_destinations.needs: Proposal only: description, reasons by popularity with photos, tips, best months and a header (Pipeline C); coordinates to confirm.

spots.name: Princess Royal Fortress
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=museum 'Princess Royal Fortress' agreeing with photon
spots.bio: Hilltop fort over King George Sound, where the WWI convoys assembled, and home of the National Anzac Centre museum.
spots.reason: Albany's headline: paid fort and museum site of several hours (Wikivoyage, the board's National ANZAC Centre listing). The National Anzac Centre on the same site is this spot, not a second one; the skeptic asks whether to show it as 'National Anzac Centre' for search, left for the owner (Wikipedia's article is 'Princess Royal Fortress').

spots.name: Albany Historic Whaling Station
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=museum 'Albany‘s Historical Whaling Museum' agreeing with commons
spots.bio: Whaling station closed in 1978, now a museum with self-guided tours of its flensing decks and the Cheynes IV.
spots.reason: Half-day museum at Frenchman Bay listed by Wikivoyage Albany and the board; a city attraction reached on the road to Torndirrup, so it stays with Albany (about 10.5 km from the centre).

spots.name: Mount Clarence
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'Mount Clarence' agreeing with wiki
spots.bio: Hill above Albany with walking trails, harbour views and the Desert Mounted Corps Memorial, shipped from Port Said in 1959.
spots.reason: Town hill with trails and the memorial (Wikivoyage, board itinerary); holds the Desert Mounted Corps War Memorial candidate as one spot, as the judge ruled.

spots.name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve

pin_hint.from: resolve-pin LOW/first pass: photon leisure=nature_reserve 'Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve'

spots.bio: Reserve east of Albany with a visitor centre, trails and lookouts, where the rare Gilbert's potoroo was rediscovered.
spots.reason: A nature reserve with only two kept spots (itself and Little Beach), too few for a destination, so it goes under Albany, the base visitors reach it from (about 27 km). Pin at the visitor centre, not Little Beach.

spots.name: Little Beach
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=beach 'Little Beach' agreeing with commons

spots.reason: Board and DBCA listing; reached from Albany (about 29 km, the farthest Albany spot, inside the 30 km reach).

spots.name: Middleton Beach

pin_hint.from: resolve-pin LOW/first pass: photon place=suburb 'Middleton Beach'

spots.reason: Visit Albany's lead beach; Ellen Cove (rejected as a duplicate) is part of this spot. Its Noongar name, Binalup, can go in the bio at research.

spots.name: Museum of the Great Southern

pin_hint.from: resolve-pin LOW/first pass: commons photo median '3 geotagged files'

spots.bio: Albany's branch of the state museum, with natural and social history galleries and a full-size replica of the brig Amity.
spots.facts_source: WA Museum page via the judge: open daily 10-4, free
spots.reason: Board listing and the WA Museum's page; holds the Residency Museum (rejected as the same site) and is where the Brig Amity replica stands (Brig Amity is in review: if approved it could stay folded in here). Candidate coordinates were the Perth museum: never carried over.

spots.name: West Cape Howe National Park

pin_hint.from: resolve-pin LOW/first pass: photon leisure=nature_reserve 'West Cape Howe National Park'

spots.reason: A small park with two kept spots (itself and Shelley Beach), too few for a destination; reached from Albany (Visit Albany's national parks page), about 27 km west, inside the 30 km reach. Pin at a visitor point other than Shelley Beach (most of the park is 4WD).

pin_hint.from: resolve-pin LOW/first pass: photon highway=residential 'Shelley Beach Road'

review.name: Kojonup
review.reason: For: Australia's South West has a Kojonup destination page and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany itinerary calls it a 'popular stop'; the town has The Kodja Place and the Military Barracks museum.
review.objection: Against: its one real draw, The Kodja Place, is a separate candidate, so the town would be a wrapper beside its own attraction (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); a service stop on Albany Highway rather than a base.
review.would_go: standalone 'kojonup' (if approved; but the skeptic notes it would be a wrapper beside The Kodja Place)

review.name: Katanning All Ages Playground
review.reason: For: the Shire of Katanning's visitor page and Australia's South West's 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' both single it out as an 'iconic', free attraction with giant slides and seesaws for all ages, a known road-trip stop.
review.objection: Against: it is a playground, close to the 'ordinary suburban park' negative benchmark; the shire's own page is not independent of the board; better as a reason in Katanning's bio than its own spot.
review.would_go: standalone, or named in Katanning's bio (already is)

review.name: Brig Amity Replica
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both describe boarding the full-size replica of the 1826 settlers' brig with volunteer guides; a distinct thing to do.
review.objection: Against: Visit Albany says 'the Amity is part of the Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road', so it may be part of a larger spot (rule 3); volunteer-staffed with variable hours. Either keep it as its own spot or fold it into the Museum of the Great Southern's bio.
review.would_go: fold into albany-7 Museum of the Great Southern (already named in its bio), or albany spot

review.name: Old Post Office, Albany
review.reason: Rule 1-2: one counted source (Wikivoyage See) names it for its spiral tower stair and a museum inside; a heritage building the public can enter.
review.objection: Wikivoyage also says it now houses restaurants and a weaver; whether the museum is still open is unconfirmed, and with one source and a short visit it is marginal (a building on the Stirling Terrace heritage walk rather than a destination in itself).

review.name: Mount Melville
review.reason: For: a summit with an observation tower ('the Spark Plug') and walk trails over Albany, Princess Royal Harbour and King George Sound; Lonely Planet carried a 'Mt Melville Lookout Tower' sight (seen in search only; the page now redirects).
review.objection: Against: no counted source could be opened (Visit Albany's walks and parks pages do not name it), reviewers report the upper stairs closed and trees blocking views; Mount Clarence and Mount Adelaide are Albany's promoted lookouts.

review.name: Quaranup Point Possession Trail
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany Do listing names the 1.6 km walk from the old Quarantine Station to Point Possession, where Vancouver claimed WA for Britain; a real walk with a historic endpoint.
review.objection: Against: only one counted source, short, and not among Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks; no coordinates yet.

review.name: Goode Beach
review.reason: For: a sheltered Vancouver Peninsula beach; RAC's Albany beach guide names it as the access to Mistaken Island (walkable at low tide).
review.objection: Against: no counted source names Goode Beach itself as a place to go (Visit Albany's beaches page omits it); it is a residential suburb beach.

review.name: Muttonbird Island
review.reason: For: the visitor place here is Muttonbird Beach, which Visit Albany's beaches page lists (surfing, fishing, sheltered cove by Shelter Island) and RAC describes; keep it under that name if approved.
review.objection: Against: the candidate as named is the island, a reserve with no visitor use; the beach is 4WD-dependent for much of its length and mainly a local surf/fishing spot.

review.name: Betty's Beach
review.reason: For: RAC's Albany guide names Bettys Beach camping area (2WD access, direct beach access, 40 min east of Albany).
review.objection: Against: no counted visitor source beyond a motoring-club list; a fishing and camping beach used by professional fishermen in autumn; lean reject.
review.would_go: albany (about 35 km: at the edge; else standalone)

review.name: Torbay Head
review.reason: For: DBCA attraction page (named by Vancouver in 1792; DBCA calls it the southernmost point of WA) and Visit Albany notes West Cape Howe as WA's southern promontory; a 'southernmost point' is the kind of landmark people seek out.
review.objection: Against: reached only by 4WD or a long sandy walk, mostly seen from Shelley Beach; likely folded into West Cape Howe National Park.
review.would_go: fold into albany-9 West Cape Howe National Park

review.name: Waterfall Beach
review.reason: For: RAC's Albany guide gives it a section (secluded beach in Two Peoples Bay with a small waterfall onto the sand) and Visit Albany suggests it as a walk from Little Beach.
review.objection: Against: Visit Albany treats it as an extension of a Little Beach visit (part of a larger spot), no counted page of its own. Note: DBCA's 'Waterfall Beach' page is a different place in William Bay NP near Denmark, which the enumeration may have missed and should be judged on its own.
review.would_go: fold into albany-5 Little Beach (note the different William Bay Waterfall Beach)

review.name: St Mary Inlet
review.reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page names it (scenic inlet behind the dunes near Point Ann, birdwatching, shore walk at low water, campground). Case for: a named visitor site with a campground listed by Wikivoyage. Case against: rule 3, it sits beside Point Ann (the park's whale-watching point) and may be part of that visit rather than a distinct draw.
review.objection: No formal paths; the visit is mainly camping or a look on the way to Point Ann.

review.name: Hakea Trail
review.reason: Rule 1: named only as a DBCA gallery caption and as the foot route to Whalebone Beach; DBCA has no trail page for it (exploreparks /trail/hakea-trail 404). Case for: a coastal walk through the park's plant diversity linking Quoin Head and Whalebone Beach. Case against: one weak mention, and rule 3, it may be best folded into Whalebone Beach/Quoin Head.
review.objection: No length, trailhead or trail page found; a gallery caption is a thin source.

review.name: Dillon Bay
review.reason: Re-looked: no counted source found (only ExplorOz, BeachSafe and campsite directories, plus Wikipedia's Bremer Bay page). Case for: a sheltered bay south of Bremer Bay with Blossoms Beach (4WD beach driving), camping and fishing, partly in Fitzgerald River NP. Case against: rule 1 fails without a visitor-oriented source; it reads as a locals' fishing spot.
review.objection: No tourism board, DBCA or guidebook names it; ExplorOz and BeachSafe are not counted sources.

review.name: Denmark Historical Museum
review.reason: Rule 1: one counted source, a Wikivoyage See listing (16 Mitchell St, local history of Denmark's timber and industrial times). Case for: open to the public, a half-hour indoor visit. Case against: a small volunteer local-history museum with limited hours; the friend test says only if nearby, and it needs a second source.
review.objection: Single source, short visit, local interest only.

review.name: Hilltop Lookout
review.reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre name it (forest-clearing view over the Frankland River, Nornalup Inlet and the Southern Ocean). Case for: two sources and a real view. Case against: rule 3, a short stop on the same one-way Hilltop Road as the Giant Tingle Tree, about 1 km apart; could be folded into that spot.
review.objection: A ten-minute look on the way to the Giant Tingle Tree.
review.would_go: walpole-wilderness (or fold into Giant Tingle Tree)

review.name: Irwin Inlet
review.reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page only (picnic, boating and fishing; sand spit reached by 4WD from Peaceful Bay). Case for: a named DBCA visitor site. Case against: one source, and visitors mostly reach it from Peaceful Bay, which is kept; a quiet fishing spot rather than a draw.
review.objection: Locals' fishing spot; overlaps Peaceful Bay.

review.name: Stirling Range Scenic Drive
review.reason: Rule 1: DBCA's Stirling Range park page names the 42 km mostly unsealed scenic drive through the heart of the park with stops. Case for: the main non-hiking way to see the range, a real half-day outing. Case against: 'a spot is a place': a road, whose stops (peaks, lookouts, picnic areas) are the places; it overlaps the park itself.
review.objection: Drives are routes, not places; it duplicates the park.
review.would_go: fold into stirling-range-national-park description (a road, not a place)

review.name: Cape Riche
review.reason: Re-looked: one counted source, Visit Albany's (amazingalbany.com.au) nature-based camping page, which names Cape Riche as a caretaker-run campground; the City of Albany camping page agrees. Case for: a remote cape for fishing, swimming, snorkelling, headland rock walks and Mount Melville. Case against: named only as a campground, no source describes a sight; one source.
review.objection: A campground listing is not a visitor 'See' entry; mostly anglers and campers.

review.name: Oyster Harbour
review.reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (swimming beaches, picnic areas, fishing, boat cruises up the Kalgan River). Case for: a counted source naming it as a family outing. Case against: rule 3, the harbour is a water body visited from Emu Point on its southern shore (kept); as a spot it is a near-duplicate of Emu Point.
review.objection: Its visitor point is Emu Point.

review.name: Denmark Animal Farm and Pentland Alpaca Stud
review.reason: Rule 1: Australia's South West board listing and its own site (animal park, open every day 10-4, WA's first alpaca farm, about 50 alpacas). Case for: a permanent, open, family visitor farm. Case against: rule 2/business: largely a gift shop and petting farm, and the friend test says only if nearby; one source.
review.objection: A small commercial farm attraction with a shop.

review.name: Wilson Inlet
review.reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (paddling, kayak and canoe hire, fishing, the 12 km Wilson Inlet Heritage Trail to Crusoe Beach, inlet cruises). Case for: a counted source and a range of things to do. Case against: rule 3, a water body whose visitor points are Ocean Beach (kept) and Denmark's riverfront; the Heritage Trail might be the better spot.
review.objection: A 20 km water body has no single visitor point; overlaps Ocean Beach.

duplicates_elsewhere.name: Bibbulmun Track
duplicates_elsewhere.why: Run-wide decision: long trails placed once, at the midpoint of the whole route. Its southern terminus is Albany and it passes Walpole, Denmark and West Cape Howe: mention it in those destinations' descriptions.

duplicates_elsewhere.name: Munda Biddi Trail
duplicates_elsewhere.why: Run-wide decision; it ends in Albany.

standalone_neighbour_check.why_not_a_spot: Outside Albany's 30 km reach (75% of 40 km) and reached via Mount Barker on its own trip, not around the city; widening Albany to about 52 km to take in the range would balloon a city span. A park is its own place, not a city's.
A national park is never a spot of another national park (COVERAGE 'park-in-park'); also beyond the Stirling span's 34 km reach.
Part of the Porongurup group: outside Albany's 30 km reach and reached from Mount Barker or the Porongurup village, not the city.
44 km north of the park, in a different park (Porongurup); never a spot of Torndirrup.
It is in Porongurup National Park, a different park; a walk of one park is never a spot of another.
Part of the Porongurup group: outside Albany's 30 km reach and reached from Mount Barker, not the city.
It is in Porongurup National Park, a different park; never a spot of the Stirling Range.

A town outside the park, about 42 km from its reference point and beyond its 34 km reach; a town is not a spot of a park it lies outside. It is the gateway, closer to the Porongurups than to any Stirling spot.

cross_region_notes: Walpole Wilderness span (centre Walpole, 32 km, reach 24 km) contains three wa-south-west standalones that the Walpole Visitor Centre lists under 'the Walpole Wilderness': Mandalay Beach (about 19.5 km W, D'Entrecasteaux NP), Fernhook Falls (about 22 km N, Mount Frankland South NP) and Mount Frankland National Park. They are reached from Walpole, not from the South West's destinations, so the reconciler should consider making them spots of walpole-wilderness (it is a named region, not a park, so the park-in-park rule does not bar Mount Frankland NP). Not changed here: they are wa-south-west's entries.
Hopetoun (wa-golden-outback) is the eastern gateway to Fitzgerald River NP and East Mount Barren; it is outside this destination's span.
Gould Island, Hellfire Bay and Puntapin Rock were judged outside this region (wa-golden-outback); Honeymoon Pool, Fernhook Falls, Mandalay Beach and Mount Frankland NP belong to wa-south-west.
notes: Western Australia has no destinations or spots in the app yet, so there are no existing spots to move. Pins: resolve-pin.py was run for every spot; HIGH points are recorded, everything else is null with needs_research 'coordinates' and, where one was found, a pin_hint (a LOW first-pass feature, never to be used as is). Overpass was down and Photon throttled during the run, so many LOW results are source outages, not missing features. Museum of the Great Southern's enumerator point (Perth) was not carried over. Hours, costs and most ticket links are left for Pipeline C; ticketUrls given are DBCA pages whose titles were checked to name the place (The Gap's DBCA site URL is a 404, so the park page is used). Destination category for Denmark is 'beach' (its draws are coastal); change to 'city' if the owner prefers. No copy names a source.
